Italian Fried Pasta

A super delicious way to enjoy pasta!

September 9, 2026September 9, 2026
5 from 6 reviews

Italian Fried Pasta is crispy, salty, cheesy – and ridiculously good!

After one bite of our Italian Fried Pasta – I predict – you won’t be able to stop eating it!

The inspiration for this Italian Fried Pasta recipe came from a Facebook group that Jack and I both follow that’s centered around homemade Italian recipes. That group is a treasure-trove of old family recipes, and someone happened to mention that their parents used to fry up leftover cooked pasta and sprinkle it with cheese.

As soon as that fried pasta was mentioned, a number of other group members chimed in – some families added cured meats, others added different seasonings and dried herbs. Every suggestion sounded delicious – so we decided to give it a try!

This Italian Fried Pasta is salty and savory – and after one taste, you’ll want to devour it!

It’s satisfying comfort food on its own – or you can serve it as a side dish with our Italian Pot Roast.

Italian Fried Pasta is ridiculously good – and I can’t believe I had never heard of it before! If you love eating the crispy, slightly crunchy edges of a baked macaroni and cheese or these mac and cheese cupcakes – this is similar, but better!

What kind of pasta should I use for Italian Fried Pasta?

For this recipe, ideally, you want a pasta that will allow some edges to touch the pan as it fries, while others will remain un-fried.

We used cavatappi, which is a spiral macaroni. But bow-ties (aka farfalle) would also work, or any other sturdy pasta shape with different textures and edges works best.

Key Ingredients & Substitutions

  • Pasta – As mentioned above, use a sturdy pasta such as cavatappi or farfalle.
  • Extra Virgin Olive Oil
  • Red Pepper Flakes
  • Fresh Garlic
  • Other Seasonings – Including Kosher salt, ground black pepper, dried basil and dried oregano.
  • Genoa Salami – Or other cured meats just as prosciutto.
  • Cheeses – Including Parmesan and Romano.

“This recipe is absolutely delicious!! We’ve made it twice so far but it is going to be in our rotation for sure!” – Julie

How do you make Italian Fried Pasta?

  1. First, you’ll cook your favorite pasta in salted water, just shy of al dente. You want the pasta to be a bit chewy. Pour the pasta into a strainer, rinse it with cold water, then allow it to drain completely.
  2. Next, pour the pasta onto a large sheet pan, then use paper towels to blot off any remaining moisture. Once it is dry – pour the pasta back into the pot you first cooked it in (there should be no water left in the pan) and season with kosher salt, freshly ground black pepper, dry basil, and dry oregano.
  3. Heat oil in a large skillet (or even a wok), then add a pinch of red pepper flakes and some whole garlic cloves. Cook the garlic in the seasoned oil, turning frequently so that the outside gets lightly browned, and the inside is soft and tender. Remove the garlic to a cutting board and dice finely.
  4. Next, fry the cooked pasta in two batches. First – add some chopped, diced Genoa salami to the skillet along with half the pasta. Toss and turn the pasta so it fries evenly, but also allowing it to brown and crisp up in spots. This will take about five to ten minutes per batch. Place the fried pasta in large bowl and sprinkle with grated Parmesan and Romano cheeses. (Repeat until all of the pasta is fried.)
  5. Finally, toss in the previously cooked garlic – and you are ready to serve.

Italian Fried Pasta is crispy, salty, cheesy – and ridiculously good!

  • Author: A Family Feast
  • Prep Time: 10 minutes
  • Cook Time: 20 minutes
  • Total Time: 30 minutes
  • Yield: 8 servings 1x
  • Category: Side Dish
  • Method: fried
  • Cuisine: Italian

Ingredients

Scale

1 pound spiral macaroni (Cavatappi), or your favorite pasta

1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil

Pinch red pepper flakes

4 large garlic cloves, peeled and left whole

1 teaspoon kosher salt

1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

1 teaspoon dry basil

1 teaspoon dry oregano

1/4 pound Genoa salami, diced small, divided

1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese

1/2 cup grated Romano cheese

Instructions

  1. Cook pasta in salted water to about two minutes less than done. (Still a bit chewy). Pour into a strainer, cool with cold water and drain completely.
  2. Line a sheet tray with paper towels and pour drained pasta on top and cover with more paper towels to absorb most of the water.
  3. In a wide heavy bottomed saute pan or wok, heat oil over medium low heat and add pepper flakes and garlic and let cook for 15 or so minutes until garlic is golden brown and soft (keep turning garlic to brown all sides). Remove cooked garlic to your cutting board and dice fine. Set that aside.
  4. Pour half of the oil into a heat proof small bowl. We will be frying the pasta in two batches and need to reserve half of the oil to do so.
  5. Pour the drained and dried pasta into the empty pan you cooked it in and toss with the salt, pepper, basil and oregano.
  6. Heat half the oil over high heat and once hot, add half of the salami and half of the seasoned pasta and fry for 5-10 minutes until some of the pasta pieces start to brown and develop a crust. I tossed mine every minute, so they had time to brown on the bottom, then I tossed and let them brown some more. Each of my batches took about eight minutes. Use a strainer or spider and remove to a large bowl and toss with half of each cheese.
  7. Heat the remaining oil and once hot, repeat the process for the salami and pasta and cheese.
  8. Add the two batches together along with the cooked chopped garlic from earlier, and pour into a serving bowl and enjoy.

This Italian Fried Pasta originally appeared on A Family Feast in January 2020. We’ve made some minor updates to the post but the original recipe remains the same.

Frequently Asked Questions

  1. Can I use fully-cooked pasta in this Fried Pasta recipe? Yes – as long as there isn’t sauce on the cooked pasta, you can use it to make this recipe. Be sure to dry the pasta completely (blot it with paper towels) first.
  2. Can I make this with bacon or pancetta? Yes – but you’ll need to cook and drain these meats first. Be sure to drain any excess fat too.
  3. Can I use an air fryer to make this fried pasta recipe? Not exactly as written. Since the air fryer is basically a small convection oven, the foods crisp up from circulating air, where as in our recipe, the bits of pasta brown and caramelize on the bottom of the hot skillet in oil to get crispy. I’d suggest following an air-fryer specific recipe if you have your heart set on using the air fryer.
